P01Platform ownership · Cost optimisation

tldv — Conversation Intelligence Evaluation & Migration

A tool replacement treated as a full lifecycle: evaluate, implement, configure, enable, save — and make the resulting data reusable.

Business problem & outcome

We were paying premium recurring cost for conversation intelligence that GTM used for a narrow set of capabilities. The renewal was approaching and nobody had tested whether the spend matched the requirement. Worse, meeting data sat in a silo — it was a recording archive, not a GTM data source.

  • Ran a structured evaluation against actual GTM workflows rather than a feature checklist, and selected tldv.
  • Owned onboarding, configuration, integration and user enablement end to end — no external implementation cost.
  • $10K annual savings realised on recurring tool spend with no loss of capability.
  • Transitioned users off the previous platform without a gap in meeting coverage.
  • Most importantly: made meeting transcripts an addressable data source feeding the Unified GTM Connector and the Synchinator pipelines.
$10KAnnual saving
0Capability lost
1New GTM data source

Tech stack & how it was delivered

  • tldv
  • HubSpot CRM integration
  • Google Calendar / Meet
  • Zoom
  • tldv API

  • Postgres + pgvector

  • Integration — calendar and conferencing connections, CRM association so meetings land on the right contact and deal records.

  • Enablement — workspace configuration, recording policies, user rollout and adoption support.

P02AI intelligence · Flagship

Unified GTM Custom Connector

One AI-accessible query surface over CRM, email, meetings, product usage and collateral — the initiative I am most proud of, because it created a foundation rather than a feature.

Business problem & outcome

Answering an ordinary GTM question — "what is happening in this account?" — meant opening the CRM, searching email, finding the meeting recording, checking product usage, then reconciling it all by hand. The information existed; the assembly cost was the bottleneck. Every analysis was therefore expensive, inconsistent, and rarely repeated.

  • Changed the interaction model from find the system → search the record → compare fields to ask the question → get the assembled answer.
  • 10+ distinct GTM use cases delivered on the same layer — account research, deal-stage analysis, customer department and use-case discovery, conversation history, collateral search.
  • Made it possible to check CRM values against what was actually said in meetings and done in the product — surfacing records that need human review.
  • Cut time-to-insight for account and deal research from hours of manual navigation to a single question.
  • Reusable by design: each new use case is a prompt and a view, not a new integration project.

P02cThe connector in practice

S0 Deal Intelligence Report — MEA pipeline

A real output, not a mockup. The connector read the CRM, the email log and the meeting record together, and explained why three MEA deals were stuck at S0 — something no single system could answer.

Kissflow RevOps · refreshed 22 July 2026 Focus deals: Modern Chemicals & Services · Set4solutions · Vision Bank Source conversation ↗
WHAT IT DID

Cross-checked the record against reality

Compared each deal's CRM state — stage, close date, owner, last activity — against the actual email log and meeting history, and reported where the two disagreed.

WHAT IT FOUND

Five systemic issues, not five anecdotes

A closing RFP window with six weeks of email silence. An agreed follow-up call that never happened. A live conversation on a deal with no AE and a close date already in the past.

WHY IT MATTERS

The forecast was wrong in a knowable way

Active evaluation work was invisible in the pipeline, and last-activity dates disagreed with the email log — so RevOps could not tell a stalled deal from an unlogged one, and alerts fired on the wrong deals.

P02dThe connector in practice · Marketing enablement

ERP Orchestration — real customer use cases, cleared for publication

Marketing asked for real proof points for an ERP orchestration landing page. The connector answered from what customers actually said in meetings, cross-checked each account against the CRM, and — the part that matters — flagged which stories are legally safe to publish.

Prepared 10 July 2026 · sources: ProShort meeting intelligence + HubSpot CRM 10 accounts · 5 ERP systems · 5 regions
THE ASK

A marketing question in plain English

"Give me the real customer use cases where we delivered ERP orchestration value — customer, region, ERP, use case, and three lines on how they saw the value." No spec, no ticket, no SQL.

WHERE THE ANSWER CAME FROM

What customers actually said

Value descriptions are drawn from ProShort meeting intelligence — customers in their own words — not modelled ROI figures. SAP, Oracle EBS, NetSuite, Dynamics 365 and JD Edwards, across NAM, EMEA, MEA, APAC and India.

THE GOVERNANCE LAYER

Every story carries a clearance status

Each account was checked against HubSpot for customer status and reference clearance: 6 cleared for website and press, 3 needing owner confirmation with the account owner named, and 1 contractually barred from publication.

WHY IT MATTERS

Days of chasing, answered in one question

This normally means asking AEs and CSMs, digging through call notes, then chasing legal for reference rights. More importantly, the clearance column is what stops a contractually barred logo reaching a public landing page.

P03Recently built · Live in production

Data Enrichment Portal — the inversion

The system researches first; the human validates. A three-person manual research function becomes a validation function — and for the first time, a measured one.

Business problem & outcome

Three people on the Data Mining team hand-enrich 20–25 HubSpot signups every day — job title, company size, revenue, industry, location — across Apollo, ZoomInfo, LinkedIn and web search, then type the result into the CRM. Three consequences: it does not scale (headcount is the only lever), it is unmeasured (nobody knows how much is right, or which vendor is worth paying for), and the CRM keeps no provenance — a value is just a value, with no source, date or confidence.

  • The job changes from research to validation — confirm, correct, or fill. Nothing reaches the CRM without a person approving it.
  • Live and in daily use by the team for the past month, with 500+ prospect and company records enriched so far.
  • Capacity is decoupled from headcount: signup volume can grow without adding researchers.
  • Every field carries provenance — which vendor supplied it, when, and with what confidence.
  • Management can finally answer the question that was previously unanswerable: how much did the system get right unaided, versus what humans corrected or added — per field, per vendor, per reviewer.
  • Reviewer workflow built for speed: high-confidence rows collapse to one line, keyboard-driven, only ambiguous fields cost a keystroke.
  • AI spend held under $50/month by hard design — a circuit breaker, not a budget alert.

P03bThe reviewer's screen

Inside the app — what a reviewer actually sees

The whole design goal on one screen: the system has already done the research, and the reviewer's only job is to agree, correct, or fill — with the evidence for every value sitting right next to it.

Data Enrichment · Review queueLive in production since August 2026
01 · THE QUEUE

Work arrives sorted

Contacts are grouped into Needs you, Conflicts and Overwrites, each showing how many fields still need a decision, so the reviewer never chooses what to work on next.

02 · THE PROPOSAL

Every value shows its source and confidence

Each field carries the vendor that supplied it and a confidence score. Fields already correct in HubSpot collapse away; fields no source could find are grouped separately to be filled by hand.

03 · THE EVIDENCE

Disagreements are shown, not hidden

The evidence panel shows what each vendor reported, what HubSpot currently holds, and how the confidence score was reached — including the penalty applied when sources disagree.

04 · THE DECISION

A person always submits

Accept, edit or reject per field, then submit to HubSpot in one action. The system proposes; the human decides; the CRM only ever receives approved values.

SaaS / Software Subscription Request Application

Turning scattered software purchasing into a governed process with a single spend picture across the departments that buy software.

Business problem & outcome

Software was being requested, approved and renewed through email and conversation. There was no consistent record of what we buy, who owns it, what it costs, or when it renews — which made both budgeting and rationalisation guesswork, and let duplicate tools accumulate quietly across departments.

  • Departmental spend and forward projections now reportable — finance can plan instead of reconcile.
  • Created the evidence base for rationalisation: duplicate tooling, low-usage licences and renewal decisions are now discussable with data.

P05Customer operations

KLM Application — Expanded Business Capabilities

Extended an existing internal application into the post-sale motion: service requests, add-ons and customer feature management.

Changes for existing customers — enabling a feature, adding a service, provisioning an add-on — were being coordinated person to person over chat and email. P06Relationship intelligence

Customer Champion Job Change Intelligence

Turning a static CRM contact record into a live relationship signal — and a champion's move into a pipeline opportunity.

Business problem & outcome

Champions are the strongest relationship asset in an account — and the most perishable. When one changes role, department or company, the CRM keeps showing the old title indefinitely. Two things are lost at once: the account quietly loses its internal advocate, and a warm buyer walks into a new company where nobody is following up. Both were being discovered months late, by accident.

  • Built a workflow that identified 500+ champion job and company changes and routed them to the owning Account Manager.
  • Retention play: champion moves internally → AM is alerted → identify the new decision-maker → re-establish coverage before renewal.
  • Expansion play: champion joins a new company → a pre-qualified prospect with a known relationship and a known product preference.
  • Converted an invisible, unmanaged risk into a routine, actionable queue.
  • Feeds directly into the churn-risk and whitespace models planned for next year.
500+Changes surfaced

Tech stack & how it was built

  • Apollo / ZoomInfo signals

P07Data integration layer

Zoho Synchinator — Complete Revamp

Rebuilt our sync utility into a dependable GTM data integration layer — better to operate, harder to break, and carrying more of the business.

Business problem & outcome

Every dashboard, report and AI use case downstream depends on the sync being correct and on time. The existing Synchinator worked, but it was opaque to operate — when something failed, diagnosis meant reading logs — and its sync objects had accumulated fragility. A silent sync failure looks exactly like a quiet week in the business, which is the most expensive kind of data problem.

  • Rebuilt the interface so sync state, failures and history are legible to an operator rather than an engineer.
  • Hardened existing sync objects — reviewed each one, improved durability and strengthened the underlying sync architecture.
  • Added new data pipelines: HubSpot Notetaker mapping, Participants master list, HubSpot Meetings master list, and the tldv meetings pipeline.
  • Meeting and participant data became first-class synced objects — which is precisely what made the Unified GTM Connector's conversation intelligence possible.
  • The Synchinator stopped being a utility and became the integration layer the GTM stack sits on.

P08Cross-functional · Product-led GTM

Product Data Partnership — Usage Intelligence

Worked with Product to make usage data accurate, available and GTM-shaped — the missing fourth signal behind product-led revenue motion.

Business problem & outcome

GTM could see who the customer is, what they say and what we send them — but not what they actually use. Product usage existed, but not in a form GTM could act on: gaps in coverage, accuracy issues, and metrics defined for engineering rather than for revenue conversations. Without it, expansion and churn conversations were based on sentiment.

  • Brought AI usage, 2.0 customer usage, user metadata, flow metadata and Smart Attachments signals into the GTM data architecture.
  • Identified and closed gaps in existing data, and worked with Product on accuracy rather than accepting what was available.
  • Specified the new data points GTM actually needs — defined from the revenue question backwards, not from what happened to be instrumented.
  • Completed the picture: who the customer is + what they are saying + what they are doing + what they are actually using.
  • This is the foundation for product-led GTM intelligence — adoption-based expansion signals and usage-decline churn risk both depend on it.

P09Enablement · Capability spread

RevOps AI Enablement — Claude Hands-on Sessions

AI capability that lives only in the technology team is a bottleneck, not a capability. This was about moving it outward.

Business problem & outcome

Every AI-assisted analysis, validation check and research task ran through me. That is a flattering position and a terrible operating model: it caps throughput at one person's calendar, and it means the people closest to the business problem cannot test their own ideas. The constraint was not the technology — it was that nobody else had seen how to use it.

  • Ran hands-on working sessions with the RevOps team — 3+ users trained directly, using their own live problems rather than demo data.
  • Taught the parts that actually matter: how to structure a prompt, how to supply context, how to use connected data, how to turn a repeated task into an assisted workflow.
  • Team members began running their own data-quality checks, research and analysis workflows.
  • Reduced dependency on the technology team for small problems — freeing capacity for platform work.
  • Shifted the default question from "who can do this for me?" to "can AI solve this?" before manual work starts.

P10Platform · 90% complete

GTM Tribe — one address for every GTM application

Twenty-two micro-apps built across Cloud Run and Firebase, previously twenty-two unmemorable URLs. Now a single directory at gtmtribe.kissflow.net, with each app served at /apps/<slug> — and not one of them rewritten or rehosted.

Business problem & outcome

We had been shipping micro-apps quickly — dashboards, validation boards, org charts, ROI studies — and every one landed on its own generated Cloud Run or Firebase URL. The result was a shadow portfolio: real tools nobody could find. New joiners never learned they existed, work got rebuilt because the first version was unfindable, and there was no inventory of what we owned or who used it. Discoverability, not capability, had become the constraint on adoption.

  • 22 applications published behind one domain, organised into three categories — GTM Team, Marketing and RevOps — with search, filters and a "needs setup" state on anything not yet fully routed.
  • Nothing was rewritten. Each app stays exactly where it runs; a path-based load balancer route is all that changes. Migration risk is close to zero.
  • Adding an app is a form, not a deploy — the admin console writes the registry, so RevOps can publish a new tool without engineering time.
  • Gave the organisation, for the first time, a real inventory of what GTM technology exists — the same governance win the SaaS application delivered for purchased software, now for what we built ourselves.
  • Establishes the front door for next year: every Zoho dashboard we replace with an application lands here on day one.
22Apps published
1Domain

90%Complete

Tech stack & how it was built

  • Google Cloud external HTTPS LB
  • URL map + path routing
  • Serverless NEGs
  • Cloud Run
  • Firebase Hosting
  • Google-managed TLS certificate
  • Cloudflare DNS
  • Node.js portal (zero dependency)
  • GCS registry (apps.json)
  • Google Sign-In / IAP
  • Docker
  • Idempotent provisioning scripts
  • One registry drives everything. A single apps.json in Cloud Storage generates both the portal tiles and the load balancer URL map — an app is added in one place and appears in both.
  • Path-based routing, not rehosting. The URL map sends /apps/<slug> to that app's serverless NEG; Firebase-hosted apps that the load balancer cannot reach are proxied through the portal instead.
  • Admin console writes the registry live — add, rename, recategorise and reorder tiles with no rebuild and no redeploy, backed by Google Sign-In.
  • The real migration work is per-app base paths. Apps emit root-absolute redirects, so each needs a build-time base path before it serves correctly under a sub-path — done one at a time, with unmigrated slugs falling through to the portal rather than erroring.
  • Infrastructure as re-runnable scripts. NEGs, backends, certificate, URL map and rules provisioned idempotently, plus a verify script that probes every route and explains what it finds.
  • apps.json → gen-urlmap → LB URL map → /apps/<slug> → serverless NEG → Cloud Run / Firebase
P10bThe front door, live

gtmtribe.kissflow.net — 22 apps, three categories, one search box

05Reflection

What this year taught me

Build foundations, not features

The Unified GTM Connector took longer than any single use case would have, and then carried ten of them. The SaaS and KLM applications behaved the same way. Reusability is the difference between shipping work and building leverage.

Data availability sets the ceiling on AI

Every AI capability I delivered was gated by whether the underlying data existed, was accurate, and was reachable. The Synchinator revamp and the Product data partnership were not side projects — they were the precondition.

Measure the system, or you are guessing

The enrichment portal writes a provenance row even when it finds nothing, purely so the accuracy denominator is real. Designing for measurement up front is what turns "the AI seems good" into a number you can act on.

Adoption is the harder half

The SaaS application rollout and the hands-on AI sessions taught the same lesson: the implementation is the cheap part. Something used by three people is worth less than something simpler used by three hundred.

Verify against reality, not documentation

Vendor APIs, CRM option lists and product metrics all differed from what the docs and the prior art claimed. Nearly every serious bug this year came from trusting a description instead of checking the live system.

Cost control belongs in the design

AI spend is not a budgeting problem, it is an architecture problem. Recording cost before the call and stepping the breaker down in tiers is what makes an AI workload safe to leave running.

PRIORITY 02Platform migration

Migrate Zoho dashboards to standalone applications

Our reporting layer is a set of Zoho Analytics dashboards. The data underneath them is already ours, already in Postgres, already synced. The dashboards are the only rented part.

Business problem & intended outcome

Dashboards are where analysis goes to stop. A user can see that pipeline slipped — but cannot act on it in the same place, cannot ask a follow-up question, and cannot write anything back. Meanwhile every additional viewer carries a licence cost, report logic accumulates inside a tool nobody else can maintain, and the AI layer we built this year cannot reach any of it.

  • Replace rented dashboards with owned applications — purpose-built for the job each team actually does, not a chart grid.
  • Remove per-viewer licence cost as a barrier to giving people data, and reduce recurring analytics spend.
  • Make reporting actionable — write-back, task creation and record updates from inside the same screen where the problem is spotted.
  • Make it AI-native — every app sits on the same Postgres the Unified GTM Connector reads, so "explain this variance" is a question, not a follow-up meeting.
  • Own the logic — metric definitions in version control and reviewable, instead of inside a proprietary report builder.
5Target applications
0Per-viewer licences
Q1–Q4Phased, dual-run

Target stack & migration approach

  • React + TypeScript
  • Vite · Tailwind
  • Recharts
  • FastAPI (Python)
  • Postgres / pgvector
  • Google Cloud Run
  • Google SSO + RBAC
  • Zoho Synchinator pipelines
  • Unified GTM Connector
  • Kissflow (workflow apps)
  • Reuse the pattern that already works — the Data Enrichment Portal is the reference architecture: FastAPI + React on Cloud Run over the existing Postgres instance.
  • Candidate applications: pipeline & forecast, marketing attribution, customer 360 / health, GTM data-quality control room, and the existing SaaS spend app as the template.
  • Prioritise by usage × business value — instrument current dashboard usage first, then rebuild the ones people actually open. Retire the long tail rather than porting it.
  • Every new app ships onto GTM Tribe — a registry entry and a load balancer route, so it is discoverable from the day it exists.
  • Dual-run before cutover — new app and old dashboard side by side until the numbers reconcile, then retire the dashboard and its licences.
  • inventory → usage telemetry → rank by usage × value → rebuild top N → dual-run & reconcile → cut over → retire licences

Not by projects delivered. By what changed in the business because of them — with a baseline captured before each initiative goes live.

  • Manual workflows eliminated count

  • Time-to-insight minutes

Cost

Data

GTM impact

ENDClosing
This year I moved RevOps technology from a support function to an intelligence function.

I worked across systems, data, AI, integrations, applications and enablement — not to implement tools, but to create reusable capability for the GTM organisation. The Unified GTM Connector is the clearest example: instead of solving one problem, it became the foundation for ten. The tldv migration combined evaluation, implementation, adoption and measurable saving. The enrichment portal inverted a manual function and made its accuracy measurable for the first time.

Next year the goal is narrower and more accountable: agents doing routine GTM work, our own applications replacing rented dashboards, and named projects attached to how the enterprise product is actually sold and marketed — each with a baseline, a target, and a number at the end of it.
